lanes.label: Unit
lanes.explain: One function or class on its own, everything around it faked.

lanes.label: Integration (real dependency)
lanes.explain: Our code against a real database or service running locally.

lanes.label: End-to-end
lanes.explain: The whole app driven the way a reader would use it.

lanes.label: Your walkthrough
lanes.explain: Steps you run by hand, where a person's eyes are the test.

requirements.label: Place a hold
requirements.sentence: A reader can place a hold on a book that is checked out, and joins the back of that book's queue.
requirements.why: Without it, readers have no way to get a popular book except by refreshing the catalogue.
requirements.wrong_when: The hold is saved but the reader is placed at the front, or the same reader is queued twice.

requirements.label: Queue order
requirements.sentence: When a book is returned, the first reader in its queue is notified and given three days to collect it.
requirements.why: Readers who waited longest must get the book first, or the queue is meaningless.
requirements.wrong_when: The notice goes out but the book is also shown as available to everyone else.

requirements.label: Cancel a hold
requirements.sentence: A reader can cancel a hold, and everyone behind them moves up one place.
requirements.why: Stale holds block the queue for people who still want the book.
requirements.wrong_when: The hold disappears from the reader's list but still takes a place in the queue.

requirements.label: Hold limit
requirements.sentence: A reader can have at most five active holds at once.
requirements.why: An unbounded queue lets one reader lock up the popular shelf.
requirements.wrong_when: The limit is checked in the interface but a direct request can still add a sixth.

parts.label: Hold queue
parts.what: The ordered list of readers waiting for one book.

parts.label: Hold store
parts.what: The database table that keeps holds between restarts.

parts.label: Notifier
parts.what: Sends the reader a message when a book is ready.

parts.label: Clock
parts.what: Supplies the current time for the three-day pickup window.

parts.label: Holds API
parts.what: The web endpoints the interface calls.

tests.name: A new hold goes to the back of the queue
tests.passing_tells: The queue puts a new reader last. It does not tell you the hold is saved.

tests.name: The same reader cannot queue twice for one book
tests.passing_tells: A second hold by the same reader is refused by the queue logic.

tests.name: A saved hold survives a restart
tests.passing_tells: Holds written to a real local database come back in the same order.

tests.name: A return notifies only the first reader
tests.passing_tells: One message is sent, to the reader at the head of the queue.

tests.name: The pickup window closes after three days
tests.passing_tells: With a stepped clock, an uncollected book passes to the next reader on day three.

tests.name: Cancelling moves everyone behind up one place
tests.passing_tells: Through the real endpoints, positions shown to three readers update after one cancels.

steps.title: Start the app with sample data
steps.where: A terminal in the project folder
steps.why: Every later step needs a running app with a few books checked out.
steps.expected: The terminal prints "listening on :8080" and "seeded 12 books".
steps.wrong_if: It prints a connection error, or seeds fewer than 12 books.
steps.risk: Writes only to a local scratch database.

steps.title: Place two holds on one book
steps.where: The running app in a browser
steps.why: Shows the queue order a reader would actually see.
steps.instruction: Sign in as reader A and place a hold on "The Long Tide". Sign out, sign in as reader B and place a hold on the same book. Open the book page.
steps.expected: The book page lists A in position 1 and B in position 2.
steps.wrong_if: B appears first, or either reader is listed twice.
steps.risk: Writes only to the local scratch database.

steps.title: Read the real notification service's delivery log
steps.where: A terminal with read access to the shared test mail service
steps.why: Confirms the notice reaches the shared test mail service, not only our fake.
steps.expected: One entry, subject "Your hold is ready", sent within a minute of the return.
steps.wrong_if: No entry, or the notice went to reader B.
steps.risk: Read-only, but it uses your shared test mail account.

steps.title: Return the book and check the pickup deadline
steps.where: The running app in a browser
steps.why: The three-day window is the visible promise to the reader.
steps.expected: The response includes a pickup deadline exactly three days ahead.
steps.wrong_if: The deadline is missing, or the book is listed as available to all.
steps.risk: Writes only to the local scratch database.

decisions.question: Should the pickup window be tested with a stepped fake clock or by sleeping in a real run?

options.label: Stepped fake clock
options.cost: Needs the queue to accept a clock; small refactor.
options.proves: The expiry logic, instantly, but not real elapsed time.

options.label: Real sleep in a slow test
options.cost: A test that takes minutes and is flaky on busy machines.
options.proves: Real elapsed time end to end.

decisions.question: Does the hold limit count holds that are ready for pickup?

options.label: Yes, count them
options.cost: Readers at the limit cannot place new holds until they collect.

options.label: No, only waiting holds
options.cost: A reader can hold up to five plus any ready books.
options.proves: A limit on queue pressure, not on shelf pressure.

checked: Read the existing queue module and confirmed it has no clock parameter.
Confirmed a local database can be started with one command.
unchecked: Whether the shared test mail account allows reading logs from a fresh machine.
How the interface behaves with more than 200 readers in one queue.
